Evidence Summary: K2view Data Agent Builder and AI Fusion enable autonomous agents to analyze incoming context, determine which enterprise data to retrieve, sequence actions, execute dynamic Python scripts, and select tools (text-to-SQL, APIs, data services, vector search) via an MCP orchestrator without manual intervention.
Evaluation Notes: Agents execute multi-step flows and utilize automated error-handling/reflection routines to construct context.

Evidence Summary: Utilizes chain-of-thought prompt orchestration, prompt chaining, ReAct patterns, reflection, and schema-aware semantic query generation to break down complex user requests into discrete execution steps and SQL actions within an agentic RAG architecture.
Evaluation Notes: Supported by the platform's semantic enrichment, data grounding layer, and dynamic planning capabilities.

Evidence Summary: The Broadway orchestration engine coordinates multi-step business logic, data pipelines, and agent flows using configurable Stages and reusable modular Actors. K2view's MCP orchestrator plans processes, executes multi-stage data flows, and automates Data-as-a-Service delivery.
Evaluation Notes: Broadway flows can be nested, exported, and reused as discrete actors across pipelines.

Evidence Summary: K2view maintains real-time operational business context by organizing enterprise data into entity-based Micro-Databases (each customer/device maintains an isolated, always-fresh dataset) and vector stores. Its MCP orchestrator applies memory for multi-turn conversation continuity and session recall.
Evaluation Notes: Supports runtime continuity and persistent entity-level business context; does not provide a separate personal long-term memory engine.

Evidence Summary: The AI Fusion Evaluation module provides multi-turn testing frameworks, LLM-as-judge scoring (accuracy, relevance, clarity), and continuous regression testing to evaluate and refine agent prompts/performance before deployment.
Evaluation Notes: Evaluated via pre-deployment benchmark scoring and regression testing; no official evidence of autonomous continual self-training from live production interactions.

Evidence Summary: Data Agent Builder and AI Fusion support multi-agent system design and orchestration within Broadway flows, allowing specialized sub-agents and tool-calling agents to collaborate, share context, and execute tasks across structured hierarchical pipelines.
Evaluation Notes: Organizes heterogeneous sub-agents into structured, hierarchical execution paths and collaborative workflows.

Evidence Summary: K2view Data Agent Builder provides a low-code/no-code visual environment in K2studio, featuring drag-and-drop workflow assembly, prebuilt agent templates, AI-assisted data-product design, and over 200 prebuilt data-processing functions.
Evaluation Notes: Generally available visual no-code environment for rapid agent prototyping and deployment.

Evidence Summary: Features an LLM-agnostic architecture with out-of-the-box connectors for commercial and open-source models (installed via K2exchange). K2view Studio AI allows administrators to assign different models to specific agents, set model aliases, and configure fallback priority lists.
Evaluation Notes: Centralized configuration interface supports multi-LLM routing, aliases, and connector updates.

Evidence Summary: Provides a built-in chat playground, interactive visual debugging, step-by-step execution traces, live token and payload inspection, prebuilt agent templates, over 200 data functions, and centralized MCP connection setup via Studio AI.
Evaluation Notes: Accelerates testing and debugging by allowing real-time inspection of intermediate states, tokens, and data transformations.

Evidence Summary: Integrates with enterprise systems via Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP), REST/Web Service APIs, CDC, streaming message brokers, and native database connectors. Data products can expose governed business entity data directly as MCP tools.
Evaluation Notes: Native MCP server support allows LLMs to query databases, retrieve docs, and call enterprise APIs with governed context.

Evidence Summary: Supports cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP), hybrid, on-premises, and multi-cloud deployment models. Deployments are managed across Kubernetes-orchestrated container environments (via K2cloud Orchestrator), supporting data-mesh and data-fabric topologies.
Evaluation Notes: Fully covers self-hosted Kubernetes, managed cloud spaces, hybrid networks, and air-gapped on-premises deployments.

Evidence Summary: Supports human-in-the-loop controls within Broadway flows and task orchestration, enabling approval stages, role-scoped guided execution interfaces, parameter overrides, and manual review checkpoints before operations proceed.
Evaluation Notes: Administrators configure role-based approval steps and interactive checkpoints directly in data pipelines.

Evidence Summary: Observation Dashboard tracks agent activity, conversation pathways, token consumption, sentiment, satisfaction, resolution, and risk levels. AI Agent History logs requests, responses, and injected context with drill-down trace views into individual session steps.
Evaluation Notes: Delivers end-to-end operational observability, token tracking, and trace-level visibility (not formal model feature attribution).

Evidence Summary: Data security is enforced through individually 256-bit encrypted Micro-Databases, dynamic on-the-fly data masking, role-based access control (RBAC), entity-level isolation boundaries (preventing cross-entity data leakage), and complete audit logging of agent operations.
Evaluation Notes: Entity-level isolation and dynamic masking ensure strict data privacy and regulatory compliance (SOC/GDPR/HIPAA-ready).

Evidence Summary: Distributed Micro-Database architecture enables sub-second query retrieval and linearly scales across millions to billions of concurrent entities (over 4B Micro-Databases deployed; 7B+ requests served daily) handling petabyte-scale data on Kubernetes.
Evaluation Notes: Proven high-throughput scalability in tier-1 enterprise production environments.

Evidence Summary: Provides domain-specific data models and solutions for telecommunications, financial services, insurance, healthcare, and retail (e.g., Customer 360, billing inquiry automation, Customer Service Rep Assist).
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Features prebuilt entity schemas and vertical customer service solutions deployed at major telcos like Cellcom and Pelephone.

Evidence Summary: Customer deployments (e.g., Cellcom, Pelephone) demonstrate operational impacts including shorter wait/handling times, higher first-contact resolution (FCR), reduced representative ramp-up time, and accelerated AI service rollout, with rapid initial production delivery.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates quantifiable operational benefits in customer support; metrics are customer-reported rather than independently audited.
